texts.firmware.bios7_bin.about: The BIOS of the Nintendo DS's second processor (16 KB). It is usually named bios7.bin or biosnds7.bin. It is Nintendo's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.bios7i_bin.about: The BIOS of the Nintendo DSi's second processor (64 KB). It is usually named bios7i.bin or biosdsi7.bin. It holds the key the NAND image is locked with, so both have to come from the same console. It is Nintendo's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.bios9_bin.about: The BIOS of the Nintendo DS's main processor (4 KB). It is usually named bios9.bin or biosnds9.bin. It is Nintendo's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.bios9i_bin.about: The BIOS of the Nintendo DSi's main processor (64 KB). It is usually named bios9i.bin or biosdsi9.bin. It is Nintendo's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.dsi_firmware_bin.about: The firmware of a Nintendo DSi (128 KB): its wireless settings. It is usually named firmware.bin or dsifirmware.bin. It is Nintendo's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.dsi_nand_bin.about: The whole contents of a Nintendo DSi's internal memory (about 240 MB), with the console's footer at its end, as a DSi's dumping tools write it: the DSi's system, its menu and its settings. The core works on a copy in memory and never changes your file. It is Nintendo's, read from one console, and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.firmware_bin.about: The firmware of a Nintendo DS or DS Lite (128, 256 or 512 KB): the console's menu and its user settings. It is usually named firmware.bin. It is Nintendo's, with the settings of the console it was read from, and you have to supply it.
texts.setting.bios.about: Which BIOS the console's DS side starts with. 'free' is the replacement BIOS that melonDS carries: nothing has to be supplied, and most games run with it. 'original' is Nintendo's own, for the games that need it and, on a DS, for starting from the console's menu: the project then needs the DS's two BIOS files and, on a DS, its firmware file. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.boot.about: 'game' starts the game at once, as if the console's menu had just launched it. 'firmware' starts from the console's own menu, where the game is chosen by hand. On a DS that needs the BIOS setting on 'original'. On a DSi the menu is the one in the NAND image: a NAND that was never set up asks for its settings first. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.cpu.about: How the console's two ARM processors are run. 'jit' is melonDS's recompiler: it turns the game's code into code for your computer and is faster (about one and a half times in the game measured, where drawing the picture takes much of the time). 'interpreter' runs it one instruction at a time, as this core always did before this setting existed. The two count the machine's time differently, so a movie needs the same value: a project made before this setting existed was made with the interpreter, and plays back only with 'interpreter' chosen. Changing it restarts the core.
texts.setting.initialtime.about: What the console's clock shows when it is switched on, in seconds since 1970 (Unix time). The default is the first of January 2000. This is a setting, and not your computer's clock, so that a movie plays back the same on any day.
texts.setting.language.about: The language the console is set to. Many games read it to choose their own language. It replaces the language stored in a firmware file or in a DSi's NAND image. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.layout.about: How the two screens are placed in one picture. 'stacked' puts the upper screen above the lower one, as the console has them (256x384). 'side-by-side' puts them next to each other (512x192). 'top' and 'bottom' show one screen alone (256x192). It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.machine.about: Which console this project is for. 'nds' is the Nintendo DS (and DS Lite): it needs nothing but the game. 'dsi' is the Nintendo DSi, for the games made for it: it needs the DSi's two BIOS files, its firmware and a NAND image from the same console. Everything else depends on it, so changing it restarts the core.
texts.setting.rotation.about: Turns the picture clockwise by this many degrees, for the games that are played with the console held like a book. It changes the picture only; the pen still lands where the mouse points on the lower screen.
texts.setting.screen_gap.about: The number of empty pixels between the two screens, like the hinge of the console. A real console's gap is about 90. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.swap_screens.about: Exchanges the two screens in the 'stacked' and 'side-by-side' layouts: the lower screen comes first. It changes the picture only.
texts.slot.cart.help: The game's cartridge, a .nds file. A game stored as a zip has to be unpacked first. A game sold only in the DSi's shop (DSiWare) is not a cartridge and cannot be started this way.
texts.slot.savedata.help: What the cartridge's save memory holds at the start, for a project that begins from a saved game: a .sav file, as Emulator > Export Save Data... writes it and as melonDS, DeSmuME (raw saves) and BizHawk keep it. The file is never changed. Leave this empty to start with an empty cartridge.
texts.slot.savedata.name_help: a save file is identified by its extension, .sav.
